pr_body:
Support GeoJSON for points when the mapper specifies geo_point.

Closes #47815
Closes #84599
pr_comments: Hi @craigtaverner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This work was enhanced further in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85442

issue_context.title: Support GeoJson on geo_point fields
issue_context.body: geo_point field does not support GeoJson which can be a PITA if your data is in such a format. Indexing it as a geo_shape is an option but very wasteful.
comments: Docmentation added in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/86066 which will come out in 8.3.0 together with GeoJSON support for the cartesian point, done in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/85442

review_comments:
Maybe we should keep the square brackets?
```suggestion
                default -> throw new ElasticsearchParseException("[{}] must be a number", field);
```

That would be a change in behaviour. The previous code was literal `latitude must be a number`, with no square brackets, and there were tests for that. If we add square brackets, the tests fail. I think I had an intermediate version with that mistake, but fixed it when tests failed.
We need to check that we have no other elements in GeoJson (lat, lon or geohash)
Yes, I've generalized the validation now to cover all types.

This test is a duplicate of the test `testQueryPointFromMultiPointFormats` but with the number of supported formats reduced to those supported by the GeoJSON parser (so removing point as double[] and lat,lon string). This is because the current implementation added point geojson to the point parser, instead of adding point parsing to the geojson parser. The question is whether we should do it the other way round. The consequence of adding point support to the GeoJSON parser is that `geo_shape` mappers will start understanding the alternative versions of point (double[] and lat,lon string). Is that a good or a bad consequence?
I've generalized the test, keeping only test data separate (so geo_point tests all four formats, while geo_shape tests only WKT and GeoJSON).
